decisionsAlready.problem: Which nodes of the technical appendix the agent may approve on the owner's behalf, given that an approval records only the git identity it was made under.
decisionsAlready.ruling: The owner: the boundary is set by the node itself, so that the tools can check it: a node of the technical appendix with an `implements` link to an approved rule of the base specification. The independent reviewer judges every such node whose approval a commit contains, whoever approved it. The rules of the base specification, and the nodes that have no such link, are approved only by an owner.

title: A part of the specification can be read on its own

decisionsAlready.problem: Whether a domain may still be divided into several documents, and why it would be.
decisionsAlready.ruling: The owner: the permission stays. A small specification fits in one document, whose rules are grouped into sections, each with its own service information. As the system grows, the specification is divided into domains: a domain is a document of the same structure with a header of its own, usually a group of sections, sometimes a single group. A domain that grows too large, and has no logical division into smaller domains, is divided physically into files, each holding one section of the domain, so that working with it stays easy and what is loaded into the context window stays small.

decisionsAlready.problem: How a domain's document may be divided into several documents: one per section, or otherwise.
decisionsAlready.ruling: The owner: the rule sets only the lower bound. A section is the smallest unit of the division, so no document holds less than a whole section; how to divide is the owners' choice. They may give the domain's header a document of its own, or split the domain in two, the header and the first half of its sections in one document and the rest in the other.
